o-unreduced.title: о without stress
o-unreduced.body: Russian reduces unstressed о towards a: [vɐˈda]. Ukrainian doesn't, and this is the most audible mistake when coming from Russian: say вода́, never вада́. Only before a stressed /u/ does о shift slightly towards [o]. Vakulenko 2025 describes the vowel as close-mid [o] rather than /ɔ/.

sources.title: Pompino-Marschall, Steriopolo & Żygis (2017), Ukrainian, Journal of the IPA

vocative.title: The vocative
vocative.body: Russian has lost this case, apart from relics such as Боже, so here it has to become a habit: Ukrainian says ма́мо and бра́те where Russian says мама and брат. Nouns in -а usually take -о (ма́мо), soft ones -е, -є or -ю (зе́мле, Марі́є, бабу́сю). Masculine nouns usually take -е (бра́те, па́не), with г changing to ж (дру́же), or -у or -ю (си́ну, учи́телю).
